findings.title: Gallic War ends at its fourth post-Interlude Winter while the fifth remains in the deck
findings.expected: With no Faction passing a victory threshold, the fourth of five second-half Winter cards must continue through the remaining Winter phases and into the final year. The fifth second-half Winter is the last Winter and forces final scoring.
findings.observed: At the fourth second-half Winter, cumulative winter_count is 6, rebuilt played_cards contains 4 Winters, and the deck still contains 1 Winter. play_card reports is_final=true and game_over=true, performs only Victory, and leaves that fifth Winter unplayed. No Faction passes its threshold: Romans 15; Arverni 6 off-map Legions and 7 Allies/Citadels; Aedui 1; Belgae 8. Validated save/load reproduces the same outcome.
findings.cause: _count_winter_cards_in_game subtracts the rebuilt played-Winter count, then substitutes max(played Winters, cumulative resolved winter_count). Once cumulative winter_count dominates after Interlude, that substitution omits the newly drawn but unresolved current Winter. At the witnessed boundary it returns 1 + max(4,6) = 7, so resolve_winter_card's 6+1 >= 7 check ends the game even though one Winter remains in the deck.

Multiplayer threshold victories and final-Winter ranking retain their ordinary behavior.

findings.cause: victory_phase immediately finalizes any faction returned by check_any_victory. findings.title: Winter Campaign accepts repeated Battle Regions as one of its two actions
findings.expected: Each Battle Command selects Carnutes once. Winter Campaign may repeat Battle as its second Command, but each Command consumes one of the two granted actions. A response selecting the same Region twice within one Battle must remain pending for correction with board and RNG restored.
findings.observed: The public Winter Campaign validator accepts an Aedui Battle plan containing Carnutes twice and returns an action cost of 1. The public after-Harvest consumer resolves both entries, charging 2 Resources, leaving its second action available. Starting with 12 Aedui and 10 Revealed Belgae, it leaves 10 Aedui and 0 Belgae. The legal one-entry control leaves 10 Aedui and 4 Belgae and charges 1 Resource. The bad and good plans both report remaining_actions=1. A real saved SeatSession accepts and journals the repeated plan, pauses for casualty choices and its remaining action, resumes after save/load, and reproduces exactly under signature-verified replay. This reproduces with both numeric-card edition profiles and A63 in Ariovistus.
findings.cause: Winter Campaign intentionally bypasses the ordinary action wrapper to allow its printed compatibility exceptions. Its separate validator validates ownership, budget and mechanical success, but omits the unchanged Command-wide Region uniqueness constraint. The lower Battle executor treats the entries as independent Battles.

findings.observed: A saved Arverni Winter Campaign session accepts the legal Carnutes→Mandubii→Sequani March of Vercingetorix and four Warbands. On the otherwise identical ordinary Command control, the engine offers march_dropoff at Mandubii and accepts leaving two there, producing two at Mandubii and two at Sequani. Both paths cost one Resource. The durable Winter transcript contains only two winter_campaign responses; missing/invalid-input controls, rollback, save/load and signature-verified replay all pass.
findings.cause: The Winter Campaign dispatcher reuses the lower command execution path without enabling human March drop-offs. All existing physical choice/persistence machinery is present, but this paid Command entry point never invokes it.

findings.title: Roman Forced Marches has no non-player movement producer
findings.expected: Numeric32 must relocate Roman Forces using the printed Roman March priorities. In the controlled board, Provincia is the sole mobile origin and Bituriges the sole enemy-base destination; Caesar, two Legions and eighteen Auxilia can relocate there, and the Auxilia become Hidden.
findings.observed: Actual Roman dispatch selects numeric32 with its correct Roman March instruction, but public execution returns success with all twenty-one mobile pieces stationary and no game effect. The untouched Pax Gallica physical setup independently chooses and executes the same no-op. An explicit public numeric32 plan from the controlled starting board relocates all twenty-one pieces and Hides the eighteen Auxilia.
findings.cause: _derive_card_32 returns an empty dict immediately whenever faction is not Arverni. Its docstring incorrectly claims that every other NPC has No Faction instructions. The card handler defaults missing moves to an empty list and successfully finishes that empty relocation.
